chunks: 3048 - And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:
"A lame animal with a clear limp, a one-eyed animal with evident blindness, an extremely thin animal, a mangy animal, a maimed animal, or one with a broken horn should not be offered as a sacrifice."

key_terms.بِالْعَجْفَاءِ: with an emaciated, extremely thin female animal
key_terms.بِالْعَضْبَاءِ: with an animal having a broken horn or similar defect
key_terms.يُضَحَّى: to be offered as a sacrificial animal

ai.seo_question: What kinds of animals are invalid for sacrificial offering in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal conditions for animals used in sacrificial offerings, excluding those with clear physical defects. It reflects the requirement that an udhiyah be sound and free from obvious impairments.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3048 - The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said:
"A lame animal with a clear limp, a one-eyed animal with evident blindness, an extremely thin animal, a mangy animal, a maimed animal, or one with a broken horn should not be offered as a sacrifice."
